title: Effect of Weigela hortensis (Caprifoliaceae) floral morphology on pollinator behavior
decision_basis: Primary study measures corolla dimensions/accessibility and quantitatively compares nectar-robbing frequency/foraging route across sites and flower-size distributions.
notes: Eligibility frozen before formal direction coding.

title: Bird extinctions shift bill–flower trait matching in Hawaiian lobelioids
decision_basis: Primary study constructs pairwise bill-length minus flower-length trait matching and tests nectar-robbing probability with GLMMs on observed bird-flower interactions.
notes: Eligible for formal direct evidence. Not eligible for the frozen third-network k=3 lane because that preregistration requires NON_INSECTA_NON_AVES fauna.

title: Data from: Bird extinctions shift bill-flower trait matching in Hawaiian lobelioids
decision_basis: Dryad data record belongs to the Case et al. Hawaiian lobelioid study and is not an independent biological program.
notes: Link to Case_et_al_2026_Hawaii; do not increase denominator.

title: Cheaters among pollinators: Nectar robbing and thieving vary spatiotemporally with floral traits in Afrotropical forests
decision_basis: Primary paper directly relates measured floral traits to route-resolved robbing/thieving frequencies, but this biological network is already the standardized Sakhalkar network in the Letter.
notes: Do not count as an additional independent supporting program beyond its network role.

title: Cheaters among pollinators: Floral traits drive spatiotemporal variation in nectar robbing and thieving in Afrotropical rainforests
decision_basis: Preprint of the same Mount Cameroon biological study later published as Ecosphere 10.1002/ecs2.4696.

title: Asociación entre el robo de néctar y las características florales en una comunidad montana de los Andes colombianos
decision_basis: The 2013 study reports the Colombian high-Andean community later included in the broader 2016 Oikos four-community analysis; same lead author, same Cerros Orientales Bogotá Andean system, and the 2016 paper explicitly cites the 2013 analysis while extending it across 88 species/four communities.
notes: Retain as earlier subset report, not an independent biological program.
